title: RAG + Agent Quickstart Template Review Checklist (v1)
content:
Purpose
Use this checklist during PR review + release readiness for the RAG + Agent Quickstart templates (Python + TypeScript). The goal is to ship templates that are production-minded by default: safe defaults, resilient streaming, minimal lock-in, and supportable via consistent telemetry.

How to use
- Reviewer(s): DevEx owner + one Observability/SRE reviewer + Security reviewer for pre-launch gate.
- Fill out checkboxes; note deviations and link the follow-up issue.
- “Must” items are release blockers. “Should” items can ship with documented follow-ups.

Legend
[Must] Release blocker
[Should] Strongly preferred; can ship if documented and risk accepted
[Optional] Nice to have


0) Snapshot / metadata (fill in)
- Template name: ____________________  (e.g., rag-agent-python, rag-agent-typescript)
- Version stamp / release tag: ____________________
- PR(s) under review: ____________________
- Review date: ____________________
- Reviewers:
  - DevEx: ____________________
  - Observability/SRE: ____________________
  - Security: ____________________
- Notes / exceptions summary:
  - ____________________


1) Repository + file structure
1.1 Required top-level files
- [Must] README.md follows the standardized structure (quickstart → local dev → deployment → observability verification → troubleshooting)
- [Must] LICENSE present (Apache-2.0 or company-approved)
- [Must] CHANGELOG.md present OR release notes section with versioned entries
- [Must] SECURITY.md present (reporting + security expectations for templates)
- [Must] .gitignore appropriate for language (env files, virtualenvs/node_modules, local vector db data)
- [Must] .env.example included and safe (no secrets, no real endpoints)
- [Must] “Version stamp” file (e.g., .redwood-template-version or equivalent) written by CLI init
- [Should] CODEOWNERS configured (DevEx + language owner)
- [Should] CONTRIBUTING.md with local test + lint + smoke test commands

1.2 Template app structure (language specific)
Python
- [Must] Dependency spec pinned (requirements.txt with versions OR uv.lock/poetry.lock; whichever is the template standard)
- [Must] pyproject.toml includes tool config (ruff/black/mypy if used)
- [Should] src/ layout (avoid ambiguous imports) OR explicit guidance if flat structure

TypeScript
- [Must] package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock present (pinned)
- [Must] tsconfig.json present with strict-ish settings (noImplicitAny preferred)
- [Should] eslint/prettier config present OR documented formatting tool

1.3 Minimal runnable components
- [Must] Web/API entrypoint (e.g., FastAPI/Express) that demonstrates streaming generation path
- [Must] Retrieval path wired end-to-end (ingest/index OR sample prebuilt index + retrieval query)
- [Must] Agent loop present with tool calling and guardrails (max iterations, tool schema validation)
- [Must] Separate modules for: provider client, retriever interface, agent/orchestrator, observability


2) Configuration + env var schema
2.1 Env var documentation
- [Must] README lists required env vars (what/why/format) and optional env vars with defaults
- [Must] .env.example matches README and code (names + semantics)
- [Must] App fails fast with actionable error if required vars missing (not stack traces)
- [Must] No secrets printed to stdout/stderr under normal failure paths

2.2 Required env vars (minimum expected)
- [Must] REDWOOD_API_KEY (or standard API key name used by Redwood SDK)
- [Must] REDWOOD_BASE_URL / API endpoint config (for self-host / VPC / proxy scenarios); default points to hosted API
- [Must] REDWOOD_MODEL (or equivalent model identifier) supports “pinning” guidance (exact model string or versioned alias)
- [Must] OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or docs show how to run with local collector)

2.3 Optional env vars (recommended)
- [Should] REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (or equivalent)
- [Should] REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES + REDWOOD_RETRY_BACKOFF (if configurable)
- [Should] REDWOOD_MAX_TOKENS or template-level max output cap
- [Should] REDWOOD_CONCURRENCY / worker count (avoid 429s by default)
- [Should] TEMPLATE_ENV=local|staging|prod (or NODE_ENV) used for logging verbosity and exporter config
- [Should] RAG settings: chunk_size, chunk_overlap, top_k, score_threshold
- [Should] Vector store selection: local default + optional external adapter (feature-flagged)

2.4 Config validation requirements
- [Must] Validate numeric ranges (timeouts > 0, max tokens within sane limit, max iterations 1..N)
- [Must] Validate model name string non-empty; error suggests “known-good” defaults
- [Must] Validate OTEL endpoint format when enabled; include “disable telemetry locally” escape hatch
- [Must] Validation errors use stable error codes (see Error Taxonomy section) and are user-actionable


3) Observability (OpenTelemetry + Redwood conventions)
3.1 Trace basics
- [Must] Root span created per incoming request (HTTP server span) and includes correlation
- [Must] Span context propagation works across internal calls (retrieval → agent → model calls)
- [Must] Redwood request ID captured (from response headers) and attached to:
  - logs (field: redwood.request_id)
  - spans (attribute: redwood.request_id)
  - user-facing error output (when safe)
- [Must] Trace redaction rules documented; no prompt/user content exported by default

3.2 Required spans (minimum)
- [Must] rag.retrieve span (attributes: top_k, vector_store, cache_hit if applicable)
- [Must] agent.loop span (attributes: iteration_count, max_iterations)
- [Must] llm.generate span (attributes: model, streaming=true|false)
- [Must] tool.call span(s) per tool (attributes: tool.name, tool.success)
- [Should] ingestion/index span if indexing included (attributes: doc_count, chunk_count)

3.3 Required metrics (minimum)
- [Must] Request latency (end-to-end) with low-cardinality dimensions (template, route)
- [Must] Model latency (time to first token, time to last token if streaming)
- [Must] Token accounting (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens) when available
- [Must] Tool errors count + rate (by tool.name) with cardinality constraints documented
- [Must] Retrieval hit/empty results rate
- [Should] Cache hit rate (if prefix/KV caching is used/exposed)
- [Should] Retry count and final outcome metrics (success/failure)

3.4 Logging requirements
- [Must] Structured logs (JSON) with consistent fields:
  - level, message, timestamp
  - service.name / template.name / template.version
  - env (local/staging/prod)
  - redwood.request_id (when present)
  - error.code (template taxonomy)
- [Must] Redaction enabled by default (no API keys, auth headers, cookies, raw prompts, retrieved document bodies)
- [Should] Log sample event “how to verify telemetry” included in README

3.5 Cardinality and privacy checks
- [Must] No high-cardinality fields as metric labels (user_id, email, raw query, doc ids)
- [Must] If request tagging for adoption metrics exists, it’s opt-in and privacy-reviewed
- [Must] Any template telemetry header/tag is documented and safe to remove for corporate proxies


4) Safe defaults + resilience
4.1 Network defaults
- [Must] Client timeouts configured (connect + read) with documented rationale
- [Must] Retry policy safe by default (bounded retries, exponential backoff, jitter)
- [Must] Retries do NOT duplicate side effects for tool calls (idempotency guidance or explicit no-retry for tool side effects)
- [Must] Streaming disconnect handling:
  - reconnect strategy documented (what happens on partial stream)
  - ensures user gets a deterministic failure mode, not a hang
- [Should] Circuit breaker / fail-fast behavior for repeated failures (at least per process)

4.2 Cost controls
- [Must] Max tokens capped with reasonable default
- [Must] Agent max iterations capped (e.g., 3–8) + max tool output size
- [Should] Prompt size guardrail (max input length) with clear user error
- [Should] Concurrency default avoids immediate 429s for new self-serve users

4.3 RAG safety + correctness
- [Must] Retrieval empty results handled gracefully (don’t hallucinate without warning; use fallback response)
- [Must] Prompt injection guidance included (e.g., do not follow instructions from retrieved docs)
- [Should] Source attribution included (citations) OR clearly labeled as out-of-scope for v1

4.4 Error taxonomy alignment
- [Must] Errors mapped to stable codes and friendly messages:
  - AUTH_INVALID / AUTH_MISSING
  - QUOTA_RATE_LIMITED (429)
  - NETWORK_TIMEOUT
  - STREAM_DISCONNECTED
  - TOOL_SCHEMA_INVALID
  - TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED
  - RETRIEVAL_EMPTY
  - CONFIG_INVALID
- [Must] For API errors: surface HTTP status + Redwood request id (when available)
- [Should] Troubleshooting section links errors to remediation steps


5) Local development experience
5.1 One-command-ish setup
- [Must] README includes “Prereqs” and “Run locally” steps that work from a clean machine
- [Must] Local run supports:
  - loading env vars from .env
  - starting local OTel collector via docker-compose (or equivalent)
  - launching server and verifying a sample request
- [Should] “doctor” command (CLI) validates:
  - API key present
  - model configured
  - connectivity to Redwood endpoint
  - collector reachable

5.2 Sample data
- [Must] Any sample documents are non-sensitive and license-safe
- [Must] Sample data is small (fast clone + fast index)
- [Should] Provide a script for ingest/index (idempotent) with clear output

5.3 Observability verification
- [Must] README includes how to verify traces + metrics locally (where to look)
- [Should] Provide a verification script (sanity check) for emitted spans/metrics


6) Deployment notes (hosted/dedicated/private-friendly)
6.1 Deployment artifacts
- [Must] Dockerfile builds successfully and does not bake secrets
- [Must] docker-compose.yml (if provided) uses env vars, not hardcoded keys
- [Should] Example k8s manifests OR a short “deploy on k8s” guide; can be in separate docs repo
- [Should] Example for a simple PaaS (Fly.io/Render) if that’s part of v1

6.2 Runtime configuration
- [Must] Document required ports, health endpoints, and readiness behavior
- [Must] Healthcheck endpoint does not call model provider (no token burn)
- [Should] Recommended resource sizing notes (CPU/mem baseline, vector store memory considerations)

6.3 Private/VPC considerations
- [Must] Base URL override documented (for VPC/private deployments)
- [Must] TLS/proxy considerations documented for streaming (common proxy disconnect issues)
- [Should] Guidance on exporting telemetry in regulated environments (collector in-VPC)


7) Tests + CI gates
7.1 Automated checks (required)
- [Must] Lint/format check
- [Must] Dependency vulnerability scanning enabled; pinned deps with upgrade process documented
- [Must] Smoke tests cover:
  - streaming path does not hang
  - tool-call parse + schema validation
  - retrieval returns non-empty for known query
- [Should] Flake mitigation documented for streaming tests (timeouts, retries, isolation)

7.2 Release readiness
- [Must] Template versioning policy adhered to (semver-ish) and version stamp updated
- [Must] Changelog updated with user-visible changes + upgrade notes
- [Should] Release checklist includes docs link updates (“latest” vs “pinned”)


8) README content quality (consistency requirements)
- [Must] Clear “What you’ll build” section (RAG + tools + streaming) with constraints
- [Must] “Architecture overview” diagram or text description (request flow)
- [Must] “Configuration reference” section lists env vars with defaults
- [Must] “Troubleshooting” covers top issues:
  - 401 auth
  - 429 rate limit
  - streaming disconnects (proxy)
  - OTel exporter auth/endpoint issues
  - tool schema invalid
  - retrieval empty
- [Should] “Cost controls” section: max_tokens, max_iterations, concurrency suggestions
- [Should] “Observability” section: what spans/metrics emitted and how to view


9) Security / compliance mini-gate
- [Must] Secrets handling guidance included (never commit .env, use platform secrets)
- [Must] Redaction defaults verified (keys, auth headers, prompts, retrieved doc bodies)
- [Must] Dependency policy followed (pinning + scanning)
- [Must] No sample PII
- [Should] Threat model notes (prompt injection + tool abuse) in README or SECURITY.md


10) Sign-off
- DevEx sign-off: ____________________   Date: __________
- Observability/SRE sign-off: ____________________   Date: __________
- Security sign-off: ____________________   Date: __________


Appendix A: Reviewer notes template (copy/paste into PR)
- Summary:
  - ✅ (what’s ready)
  - ⚠️ (risks)
  - ❌ (blockers)
- Blockers:
  1) …
- Follow-ups (non-blocking):
  1) …
- Observability verification:
  - local collector: yes/no
  - spans present: yes/no
  - metrics present: yes/no
  - redwood.request_id present in logs: yes/no

Appendix B: Known recurring issues (FYI)
- Corporate proxies rejecting unknown headers → telemetry tagging must be opt-in and removable.
- 429s with aggressive default concurrency → keep default concurrency low and recommend scaling gradually.
- OTel exporter auth/endpoint confusion → provide clear examples and a “disable exporter locally” toggle.
- Tool schema failures → validate tool outputs and surface precise error + example fix.
